projects.title: Parallax Mendala
projects.tagline: A modular automated growing system for portable, household, and community-scale food production.
projects.story: Mendala demonstrates that Parallax can move beyond screens into practical physical systems supporting resilience, local production, education, and community use. The architecture combines modular growing chambers, rotation, water and nutrient circulation, environmental sensing, and a clear operator layer without pretending a design-stage system has already been field validated.
projects.see: The full-size and portable model families, circular operating cycle, automation stack, model comparisons, projected production, and the path toward a testable smallest prototype.
projects.proof: Master design specifications, a portable-edition specification, brochure-style product artwork, component and cost work, and production projections are known from the project archive. Their canonical public files still need to be located, reviewed, and packaged.
projects.next: Locate and publish the canonical design artifacts, then build and instrument the smallest portable prototype before making larger production claims.
projects.summary: Mendala is the clearest first example of Parallax becoming a physical product system. It begins with food resilience, but its deeper pattern is a governed, observable growing platform that can scale from a portable learning unit to a household or community installation.
projects.claimBoundary: Mendala is currently a design-stage product family. Production, yield, cost, durability, and automation figures remain projections until a physical prototype is built and measured under stated conditions.

visual.caption: A living system organized as observable cycles rather than a sealed black box.

projects.title: Graph Cinema
projects.tagline: A runtime model that treats changing graphs, admissible motion, trajectories, and continuity as the real system—not a single frozen diagram.
projects.story: Graph Cinema begins from a simple correction: a graph is one frame, while a graphfield is the world capable of producing many frames. A trajectory is the motion picture through those states, and a ledger is the continuity record explaining what moved, why it was allowed, what challenged it, and what changed. This makes history, alternatives, and repair first-class runtime objects.
projects.see: Graphframes, graphfields, typed transitions, trajectory comparison, sealed office judgments, protected dissent, continuity receipts, and replayable decision motion.
projects.proof: The core vocabulary, trajectory-first runtime concept, Agent Office separation, ledger integration, design critiques, and implementation direction have been established. A canonical visual and shell-neutral interactive demo are not yet packaged.
projects.next: Build a small deterministic viewer that can play, pause, compare, and inspect two governed trajectories over the same underlying graphfield.
projects.summary: Graph Cinema is how the Parallax Archive eventually stops behaving like a pile of pages. It lets projects be understood through movement: versions, decisions, disputes, repairs, and relationships unfolding through time.
projects.claimBoundary: Graph Cinema is an architecture and runtime design, not yet a validated general solution for graph reasoning or multi-agent governance. Demonstrations must distinguish deterministic visualization from model-generated interpretation.

visual.label: Trajectories moving through a graphfield
visual.caption: The current graph is a frame. Continuity lives in the admissible motion between frames.

projects.title: Carbon Loop
projects.tagline: A consent-based, local-first reflection and continuity system designed to strengthen human agency rather than replace it.
projects.story: Carbon Loop is the human-experience spine beneath Parallax. Its public face, LumenBridge, is intended to help a person reflect, remember, notice patterns, renew mandates, and connect computational collaboration back to real life. The system is deliberately bounded: it should support human understanding and action without claiming diagnosis, authority, consciousness, or ownership over the person using it.
projects.see: Consent and mandate renewal, local-first memory, reflective conversations, continuity records, exit rights, human councils, relationship bridges, and the boundary between support and substitution.
projects.proof: The core doctrine, Human Experience OS framing, LumenBridge public identity, consent-first architecture, local-first direction, and relationship to Parallax governance systems are established. A single canonical public introduction and demonstrable reflection loop still need packaging.
projects.next: Publish the public doctrine and claim boundary, then build a small local-first reflection loop with explicit consent, export, deletion, and no hidden authority escalation.
projects.summary: Carbon Loop is where Parallax answers the question: what is all this intelligence and infrastructure actually for? Its answer is not model autonomy. It is helping human beings retain continuity, choice, connection, and the ability to leave.
projects.claimBoundary: Carbon Loop is a design program for reflective and continuity tools. It is not therapy, diagnosis, crisis care, a substitute for relationships, or evidence that a computational system understands a person in the human sense.
